clue.text: Support was hard for current reversal

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that help was hard to come by when the tide turned against them.
explanation.definitionFit: A backwash is water flowing back, a current running in the opposite direction after a wave or a boat passes.

clue.text: Wager about second finest achievement

indicators.note: the word for a wager goes around, about, the abbreviation for second

parts.note: a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: A gambler boasts that a bet placed in seconds was their greatest triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: One's best is the top performance or record one has managed, as in a personal best.

clue.text: Cross with quest, losing every second game

indicators.note: losing every means each occurrence of the letter is dropped from the two words, three times in all

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An angry seeker abandons a hunt, dropping out half-way through a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every second' looks like alternate letters, but 'second' is S: remove every S from CROSS and QUEST, leaving CRO and QUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Croquet is a lawn game played by knocking balls through hoops with mallets.

clue.text: With which to revive plants wanting care badly?

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the two words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener asks what to use on neglected, droopy plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener uses this spouted vessel to pour water on plants and perk them up.

clue.text: Band is small and rubbish

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
tripe means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a pop group as minor and worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a narrow band of colour on a surface, as on a flag or a shirt.

clue.text: A repeated noise from screech-owl

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the bird's name, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher describes the repetitive cry of a screech-owl.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound reflected back so that it is heard again.

clue.text: Feature on a country

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A travel piece is announced: a feature article about some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a down-clue link: the facial feature sits on top of A.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the large East Asian nation.

clue.text: Upset open vessel filled with tea?

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
an urn is a large vessel for holding hot tea, as at a church fete

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over an uncovered pot of tea and makes a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to upset, in the sense of tipping something over or reversing a decision.

clue.text: Cry quietly in a public place

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet, so it stands for quietly
out means out in the open, publicly seen

explanation.surface: Someone weeps softly where others can see them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cry quietly' reads as sobbing gently, but 'quietly' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout is to call out loudly, one sense of cry.

clue.text: Again cover inner surfaces around cold lounge

indicators.note: around means the relining word is wrapped about the abbreviation for cold

parts.note: to reline is to fit a new lining again
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Decorating instructions: redo the lining of a chilly sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' looks like a room, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to lie back lazily, which is to recline.

clue.text: Link I severed with American state

parts.note: to connect is to link
cut means severed

explanation.surface: Someone describes joining things up and then cutting the tie with a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecticut is a state in New England in the north-east USA.

clue.text: Trap teen nun that's gone wild, showing no remorse

indicators.note: gone wild signals the letters of the three words run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A nun who has gone off the rails sets a trap for a teenager and feels no guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unrepentant feels no regret or contrition for what they have done.

clue.text: A problem what to do if model's facing the other way?

definitions.text: what to do if model's facing the other way?
definitions.meaning: an artist whose model has turned away must draw the model's back

explanation.surface: An art student asks what to do when the sitter turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a disadvantage, and read as two words it is sketching someone's rear view.

clue.text: Stupidly grin at sailor

indicators.note: stupidly signals that the letters of the two words are scrambled carelessly

explanation.surface: Someone grins foolishly at a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a non-commissioned sailor in the navy.

clue.text: Character left better after the bishop's gone

indicators.note: after here means what remains once the churchman has been taken away
gone tells us the abbreviation for the churchman drops out of the word better

parts.note: B is the chess-notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Things were left in a better state once the bishop departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter is a character of the alphabet.

clue.text: Rent difficulty creating a storm

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, meaning torn
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A landlord's rent problems cause a storm of protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment, but it means torn.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm.

clue.text: Information on age for distinct groups of animals

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A zoology text sets out data on how old various animal groups are.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera, plural of genus, are taxonomic groups ranking above species.

clue.text: Acquire direct current warmer as a protection against the climate

parts.note: to win is to gain or acquire
DC is the abbreviation for direct current
a heater is something that warms

explanation.surface: Buying a DC-powered heater to keep warm in a harsh climate.
explanation.walkthrough: A windcheater is a British word for a windproof jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A windcheater is a light jacket that keeps out wind and weather.

clue.text: Germany's leader entering naked jog

indicators.note: entering means the letter goes inside the word for unclothed

parts.note: nude means naked

indicators.note: the leader of the country's name is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The German chancellor goes for a run without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jog' looks like a run, but it means a gentle push.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's elbow is to give it a little push, a nudge.

clue.text: Flex with black finish

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: An electrical flex with a black end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flex' looks like a British electric cable, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To flex a limb or rod is to bend it.

clue.text: Rather slow article by Italian poet

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Dante wrote the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A dull piece of writing by an Italian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Pursue legal action around hospital

indicators.note: around means the lawsuit word goes outside the abbreviation for hospital

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit
H is the road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone means to take a hospital to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase is to run after or pursue.

clue.text: Was acquainted with contemporary sounds here

indicators.note: sounds here tells us a word for modern is heard, then written another way

parts.note: new means modern or contemporary

explanation.surface: Someone was familiar with the modern music played here.
explanation.definitionFit: To have known someone is to have been acquainted with them.

clue.text: Avoid eating fare such as hamburgers, etc

parts.note: to fast is to go without eating
fare means food

explanation.surface: Dietary advice: steer clear of burgers and similar meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamburgers are the classic example of quickly served takeaway meals.
